Q: How to force Chrome to show latest image changes on website A:

UPDATE: We now have Mod+F5 (depending on your platform, can be Ctrl, Alt, or Option - see your chrome docs for exact details, or try combinations until you find the right one. This now forces a cache-discarding reload of resources per the issues we had for this. So if you happen upon this, it is finally an option available immediately to anyone.

The other option is to expire the cache by using gnu coreutils touch <a much older date in history> filename on files that are newer or older than a certain date/time to force those files to be updated. You can use gnu coreutils find -iname PATTERN -exec touch '{}' <date> ';' to do this. Note that {} and ; must be in quotes if you do this from a shell.

(If you are using windows or OSX you can still use this, just get the Linux subsystem installed then install coreutils and a shell, I recommend zsh over the default bash as it is more flexible and works better in the subsystems.) Alternatively, you could use virtualbox to avoid SS, but that is a lot of overhead just to refresh some files.

You will likely want to automate all of this in a script, so you don't have to manually type it out. Again I recommend zsh for this, but there are plenty of other ways to do this, you need only look.

Q: How to format date column values from a database query in CodeIgniter A:

Try like this.The DATE_FORMAT() function is used to display date/time data in different formats.

SELECT DATE_FORMAT(Date,'%d-%m-%Y'), Home, HomeScore, AwayScore, Away FROM Results

For more see here http://www.w3schools.com/sql/func_date_format.asp

Q: Is there any smart way to get rid of the empty strings returned by re.split() in python? A:

re.split() results in blank strings ALL THE TIME... it's very touchy. I've experimented with your test string a lot, and can't solve the puzzle using re.split()

BUT there's a simpler way:

pattern = r"[\w\s-]+"
re.findall(pattern, x)

That will give you exactly what you want.
